text:
maya: Hey — we started seeing a small spike of 502s from the hosted API when clients hit the autocomplete endpoint. Only happens for short streaming requests (prompt ~8 tokens) and high QPS. Examples from prod: 

maya: curl -v 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/autocomplete' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"prompt":"Hel"}'
maya: response: 502 Bad Gateway, body: "upstream prematurely closed connection". x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f

samir: Thanks — can you paste a full request/response (headers + trace id) and approx time window? Also is this only autocomplete or other short streams? :eyes:

maya: Happened at 2025-11-06T14:35:09Z -> multiple clients. Only seen on /v1/autocomplete and our small chat quick-suggest route (both streaming with early finish). Attached quick curl and request id above.

samir: Got it. This smells like frontdoor/Envoy early reset on short-lived h2 streams (keepalive/conn pool churn). Do you have any customer trace ids? Any correlation with auth token rotation or a deploy?

maya: Two request ids: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f, r-0a9b8c7d6e5f. No auth rotations on that minute. There was a small console deploy ~T-3m.

deploy-bot: deploy-service: rollout finished for service=frontdoor-api at 2025-11-06T14:32:00Z (rev=stable@e3f4a) :rocket:

alex: Pinging eng-sre — we rolled frontdoor 3m before spike, could be conn rewarm. Initial hypothesis: h2 keepalive pool got drained -> new streams hit cold connections -> Envoy GFE resets on early RST_STREAM. Quick check: pool saturation and stream reset ratio in last 5m.

oncall-sre: Logs show a burst of RESET_STREAM (error: CANCEL) from envoy to upstream between 14:34:50Z and 14:36:10Z, correlation: high short-lived streams. Snippet:

oncall-sre: ```
2025-11-06T14:35:01Z frontdoor[envoy] upstream_reset: stream_id=12345 reason=CANCEL upstream=ingress-pool-7
2025-11-06T14:35:02Z frontdoor[envoy] upstream_reset: stream_id=12346 reason=CANCEL upstream=ingress-pool-3
```

samir: That aligns. Two mitigation paths: 1) increase keepalive pool / max concurrent streams per conn for frontdoor for these short flows; 2) add a small retry on 502 for autocomplete clients (idempotent-ish for short prompts) or fallback to non-streaming narrow endpoint for a few seconds. Which is acceptable for product?

julia: From support perspective, safe short-term: tell affected customers we are investigating and suggest client-side retry with jitter (2 attempts). We should avoid silent duplicates for completions though — mark as advisory.

maya: We can add a client retry now. Also can repro locally by hammering with many short sequential requests (wrk + small body). Steps I used:

maya: ```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -d '{"prompt":"Hel"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/autocomplete &
done; wait
```

alex: Nice repro. I'll try increasing keepalive settings on a canary of frontdoor and run the same hammer. Quick config patch: bump h2 max_concurrent_streams from 100 -> 300 and keepalive_idle_timeout 30s -> 60s for the canary pool. If it reduces RESET_STREAMs we can roll.

samir: Also double-check upstream ingress pool size and whether the autoscaler trimmed pools aggressively after deploy. If autoscaler removed idle VMs, that explains pool cold start + many new TLS handshakes -> resets.

oncall-sre: Confirmed autoscaler trimmed two frontdoor instances around 14:31-14:33 due to brief low utilization. Then traffic spiked and instances came back but connections were new. That matches the timeline.

julia: Plan: (1) Support advisory + client retry suggestion (maya) — done. (2) Canary change to h2 keepalive/pool (alex) — target +30 mins. (3) Monitor reset_stream ratio and 502 rate; rollback if errors increase. Owner: alex.

samir: I'll add a short-term routing rule to avoid sending autocomplete to the smallest ingress pool if possible (route to pool id > 3) until canary stable.

maya: Thanks team — letting customers know now. Will paste any more examples if they show up. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll post canary results in this thread. If you see a new 502, include x-request-id and timestamp so we can correlate.

oncall-sre: Adding dashboard alerts for upstream RESET_STREAM > 0.5% over baseline.

maya: Closing the customer ticket for now with mitigation steps and ETA. We will re-open if it recurs.
